confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on web searches done in November 2026. The figures come from crowd-sourced cost-of-living sites (Numbeo, livingcost.net, Expatistan, Finorum) and travel-guide price ranges, which ranged roughly 6-12 March-November 2026 rather than July specifically. They were in euros: cappuccino about EUR 3.8-4.0, domestic draft beer 0.5 L about EUR 5.7-6.0, inexpensive meal about EUR 15 (range 10-25), mid-range three-course meal for two about EUR 80 (range 60-100), cocktail about EUR 11 (range 8-14) and wine by the glass from about EUR 6 (up to 14 in specialist bars). I converted to USD at an assumed EUR/USD of about 1.16, which is a model estimate and was not searched. The wine glass figure has the most uncertainty among the food and drink anchors because there is little aggregated data on it. I set it near the low-to-mid part of the reported range and checked it against beer prices. The accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge only, with no searches or listings checked. They assume July peak summer and Baltic-cruise demand, which push Old Town and central rates above the yearly average. The hotel_1star_2p anchor is the least certain because Tallinn has few true budget hotels, so it relies partly on guesthouse pricing.
comparable_city_reasoning: Tallinn is a eurozone Baltic capital with heavy summer tourism. Its prices are roughly in line with Riga and Vilnius or slightly above, and well below Helsinki. Estonia's VAT increases in 2025 make it among the pricier Baltic markets. For accommodation, I used Baltic capitals in peak summer as the regional basis.
